# STM32H743 Nano FC + 4-in-1 80A ESC: Engineering Model

## 0. Scope, Assumptions, and Feasibility Finding

I don't have Job #31's requirements document, so every number below rests on the stated assumptions. Replace them with your BOM datasheet values. The equations are general. The numeric results are only as good as the inputs.

**Architecture clarification.** The STM32H743 runs ArduPilot and emits bidirectional DShot600. It does **not** do the 48 kHz commutation. Each motor's PWM is generated by an ESC MCU (assumed AT32F421 running AM32, one per motor). The H743 DMA plan (§4) and the power-stage model (§1–3) are therefore separate domains joined by four signal wires plus a current-sense line.

**Baseline assumptions:**

| Parameter | Value | Note |
|---|---|---|
| Battery | 6S, V_max = 25.2 V | worst-case switching |
| Burst phase current | 80 A RMS per motor | "80A burst" interpreted per-channel |
| MOSFET | 40 V N-ch, PDFN 3.3×3.3 | 6 per motor, 24 total |
| R_DS(on) @25 °C | 1.5 mΩ | |
| R_DS(on) temp coeff | ×1.5 at T_j = 125 °C → 2.25 mΩ | |
| t_r + t_f | 20 + 20 ns | at the chosen gate resistor |
| Q_rr | 50 nC | body diode |
| C_oss | 1.5 nF | at 25 V |
| Q_g | 30 nC @ 10 V | |
| Dead time | 100 ns per edge | |
| V_f (body diode) | 0.8 V | |
| f_sw | 48 kHz | |
| Board | 20×20 mm "nano", 8-layer, 2 oz all layers | |
| Ambient | 40 °C | |

> **Bottom-line finding (detailed in §3):** A 20×20 mm 4-in-1 cannot sustain 4×80 A. With this model, it survives roughly **1 s of simultaneous 4-motor 80 A burst from a cold start**. Continuous rating is in the single-digit-amps-per-motor range in still air and perhaps 25–35 A per motor with strong prop wash. Either the 80 A spec is a short-burst marketing number with a defined duration (which must be written into the requirements), or the form factor must grow to 30×30 mm or larger with 5×6 mm FETs.

---

## 1. Conduction Loss Model

### 1.1 Topology

The model assumes a 3-phase bridge with synchronous rectification and complementary PWM (AM32 default):

- In 6-step commutation, two phase legs carry current at any instant.
- In each conducting leg, exactly one FET is on (HS during on-time, LS during off-time, given synchronous rectification).

So the instantaneous conduction path is always **2 × R_DS(on)**, regardless of duty cycle:

$$P_{cond,ch} = 2\, I_{ph}^2\, R_{DS(on)}(T_j)$$

$$R_{DS(on)}(T_j) = R_{25}\left[1 + \alpha (T_j - 25)\right],\quad \alpha \approx 0.005\ \text{K}^{-1}$$

### 1.2 Numbers

Hot case (T_j = 125 °C, R = 2.25 mΩ):

$$P_{cond,ch} = 2 \times 80^2 \times 2.25\times10^{-3} = \mathbf{28.8\ W}$$

Cold case (25 °C, R = 1.5 mΩ): 19.2 W.

**Per FET.** Each FET conducts about 1/3 of the electrical cycle, so the time-averaged loss is:

$$P_{FET,avg} = P_{cond,ch}/6 = 4.8\ \text{W}$$

During its conduction window, the instantaneous loss is 14.4 W.

### 1.3 Electrothermal Feedback

Because R_DS(on) rises with temperature, the loss must be solved iteratively:

$$T_j = T_{board} + R_{\theta,jb}\, P_{FET}(T_j)$$

Stability condition (no thermal runaway):

$$\frac{\partial P}{\partial T}\, R_{\theta} < 1 \;\Rightarrow\; \alpha\, P_{cond}\, R_{\theta} < 1$$

With R_θ,jb ≈ 2 K/W, 0.005 × 4.8 × 2 ≈ 0.05, so the junction-to-board loop is stable. The **board-to-ambient** loop is where runaway risk lives (§3.3).

### 1.4 Other Conduction Paths (per channel at 80 A)

| Element | Assumed R | Loss |
|---|---|---|
| Phase copper, 2 oz × 4 layers, ~8 mm path | ~0.3 mΩ (×2 legs) | 3.8 W |
| Motor pad / solder joint | ~0.1 mΩ ×2 | 1.3 W |
| Battery bus (shared by 4 ch.) | 0.2 mΩ | depends on I_batt |

**Battery current.** I_batt ≈ D·I_ph per motor. At D = 0.9 and 4 motors, I_batt ≈ 288 A, which is outside any sane rating for the XT60 and wiring this class of vehicle uses. This is another indicator that "4×80 A simultaneous" is not a real operating point.

## 2. Switching Loss Model at 48 kHz

Only one leg is PWM-switching at a time in 6-step operation (the other conducting leg is held on).

### 2.1 Hard-Switching Overlap (V–I crossover)

$$P_{sw} = \tfrac{1}{2} V_{DS}\, I_{ph}\, (t_r + t_f)\, f_{sw}$$

$$= 0.5 \times 25.2 \times 80 \times 40\times10^{-9} \times 48\times10^3 = \mathbf{1.94\ W}$$

### 2.2 Dead-Time Body-Diode Conduction

$$P_{dt} = V_f\, I_{ph}\, (2 t_{dt})\, f_{sw} = 0.8 \times 80 \times 200\times10^{-9} \times 48\times10^3 = \mathbf{0.61\ W}$$

### 2.3 Reverse Recovery

$$P_{rr} = V\, Q_{rr}\, f_{sw} = 25.2 \times 50\times10^{-9} \times 48\times10^3 = 0.06\ \text{W}$$

### 2.4 Output Capacitance

$$P_{oss} = \tfrac{1}{2} C_{oss} V^2 f_{sw} \times 2 = 0.046\ \text{W}$$

### 2.5 Gate Drive (dissipated in driver and R_g, not in the FET)

$$P_g = Q_g V_{drv} f_{sw} \times 2 = 30\,\text{nC} \times 10 \times 48\,\text{k} \times 2 = 0.029\ \text{W}$$

### 2.6 Switching Summary per Channel

| Term | W |
|---|---|
| V–I overlap | 1.94 |
| Dead time | 0.61 |
| Q_rr | 0.06 |
| C_oss | 0.05 |
| **Total switching** | **≈ 2.66** |

**Sensitivity.** Switching loss scales linearly with f_sw. At 24 kHz you save about 1.3 W per channel. Conduction dominates by roughly 11:1, so frequency is not the lever. **R_DS(on) and copper are.**

### 2.7 Total Burst Dissipation

| | Per channel | 4 channels |
|---|---|---|
| FET conduction (hot) | 28.8 W | 115.2 W |
| FET switching | 2.7 W | 10.6 W |
| Copper/joints | 5.1 W | 20.4 W |
| ESC MCU + drivers + LDOs | 0.3 W | 1.2 W |
| **Total** | **36.9 W** | **≈ 147 W** |
